## Summary

- **With support restriction, TEW scatter correction and attenuation correction, the reconstructed activity is `{python} f2(S3["activity_over_truth"])`× the true activity**
  (mean reconstructed concentration in a uniform water region ÷ true concentration; 1.00 is perfect; `{python} f2(S2["activity_over_truth"])`× without attenuation correction)
- Without corrections `{python} pct(S0["outside_fraction"])` of the reconstructed activity lies outside the phantom; with all corrections `{python} pct(S3["outside_fraction"])`
- **2, 1.5 and 1 mm SRMs give the same contrast and resolution at every iteration (1 to 2,000), even on data generated with the 1 mm SRM**
- Fitted resolution (FWHM, 25.4 mm sphere, iteration 400): `{python} f1(fwhm("resolution", "2 mm", 400))` mm (2 mm SRM), `{python} f1(fwhm("resolution", "1 mm", 400))` mm (1 mm SRM)
- Recommendation: keep the 2 mm SRM (5.5× faster than 1 mm); spend effort on convergence instead

# Setup and methods

## Setup: one acquisition, SRMs at three voxel sizes

![](img/phantom_truth.png){width=100%}

| SRM grid | Non-zeros | Files (73 .npz) | In memory | Time / iteration |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 2 mm ($144^3$) | $1.43 \times 10^{9}$ | 3.2 GB | 8.6 GB, GPU | 0.2 s |
| 1.5 mm ($192^3$) | $2.24 \times 10^{9}$ | 5.0 GB | 13 GB, streamed | 0.43 s |
| 1 mm ($288^3$) | $4.61 \times 10^{9}$ | 10 GB | 28 GB, streamed | 1.1 s |

- Phantom: small Jaszczak, upside down, 25 mm below the FOV centre, 15 mCi Tc-99m in the water, 15 min
- Rods (cold PMMA): 4.8, 6.4, 7.9, 9.5, 11.1, 12.7 mm
- Spheres (cold PMMA): 6.4, 9.5, 12.7, 15.9, 19.1, 25.4 mm
- Counts (126.5–154.6 keV): 104 M recorded, 79 M after TEW, 80 M unscattered (simulation only)
- All three SRMs come from the same $1.0 \times 10^{14}$ simulated 140 keV photons
:::
::::

- Sensitivity = SRM column sum: counts detected from each voxel, per mm³ of source
- 2 mm SRM: `{python} round(sens("2mm", 2.5))` counts/mm³ at the centre, `{python} round(sens("2mm", 67.5))` at 70 mm, `{python} round(sens("2mm", 142.5))` at the FOV edge
- The three grids coincide (same photons, binned differently)
- Voxels below 1,000 counts (2 mm grid) are frozen in MLEM: support restriction
:::
::::

## Reconstruction: MLEM, and how the images are scored

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
MLEM update ($y$ = counts per detector pixel, $H$ = SRM, $\lambda$ = image):
$$\lambda_j^{(k+1)} = \frac{\lambda_j^{(k)}}{\sum_i H_{ij}} \sum_i H_{ij}\,\frac{y_i}{\sum_{j'} H_{ij'}\lambda_{j'}^{(k)}}$$

Cold contrast of an insert (1 = perfect, 0 = invisible):
$$C = 1 - \frac{\bar\lambda_{\text{insert}}}{\bar\lambda_{\text{background}}}$$

Quantitative accuracy (the "1.01×"):
$$\text{accuracy} = \frac{\bar\lambda_{\text{uniform water}}}{\lambda_{\text{true}}}, \qquad \lambda_{\text{true}} = \frac{N_{\text{phantom}}/V_{\text{water}}}{N_{\text{SRM}}/V_{\text{FOV}}}$$
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- Insert: voxels whose centre lies inside the rod or sphere
- Background, sphere: water 4–12 mm outside its surface, > 4 mm from other inserts
- Background, rods: water between the rods of the sector, > 2 mm from any rod
- Accuracy: uniform water region (z −80 to −60 mm, r < 50 mm); $N$ = simulated decays or photons, $V$ = volumes; $\lambda$ is in SRM photons per voxel
- Noise: coefficient of variation (CoV) in the same region
:::
::::

## Scatter correction (TEW): what it does

![](img/tew_spectrum.png){width=100%}

- Photons that scatter in the phantom lose energy, and many still land in the main window from the wrong direction (orange, under the grey band): `{python} mc(TW["true_scatter_main"])` of the `{python} mc(TW["main"])` main-window counts
- Two narrow side windows (green, 5.6 keV) see mostly scattered photons; TEW reads their levels and assumes the scatter falls in a straight line across the main window (red trapezoid)
- The trapezoid's area is the estimated scatter, subtracted pixel by pixel: `{python} mc(TW["tew_estimate"])`, `{python} round(100 * (TW["tew_estimate"] / TW["true_scatter_main"] - 1))` % too high here, because the photopeak's tail raises the lower window and the true scatter is not linear

## Scatter correction (TEW): the equations

All quantities are **counts in one detector pixel** $i$ (one of $73 \times 625$), from one acquisition:

$$\hat S_i = \left(\frac{C^{\text{low}}_i}{w_{\text{low}}} + \frac{C^{\text{up}}_i}{w_{\text{up}}}\right)\frac{w_{\text{main}}}{2}, \qquad y^{\text{TEW}}_i = \max\left(C^{\text{main}}_i - \hat S_i,\ 0\right)$$

- $C^{\text{main}}_i, C^{\text{low}}_i, C^{\text{up}}_i$: counts in the main (126.5–154.6 keV), lower (120.8–126.5) and upper (154.6–160.2) windows; $w$: window widths in keV (28.1, 5.6, 5.6)
- $\hat S_i$: estimated scattered counts in the main window (the trapezoid area); $y^{\text{TEW}}_i$: scatter-corrected counts, the data MLEM reconstructs
- Per pixel the estimate is noisy: a typical pixel has `{python} round(PP["median_lower"])` counts in the lower and `{python} round(PP["median_upper"])` in the upper window, so $\hat S_i$ / true scatter spans `{python} f2(PP["estimate_over_true_p10"])`–`{python} f2(PP["estimate_over_true_p90"])` (10th–90th percentile); the relative noise per pixel rises from `{python} f2(PP["median_rel_noise_raw"])` to `{python} f2(PP["median_rel_noise_tew"])`; `{python} n(PP["clipped"])` of `{python} n(PP["pixels"])` pixels go negative and are set to 0
- Planned: keep the raw counts and model the scatter in MLEM instead, comparing $y_i$ with $\sum_j H_{ij}\lambda_j + \hat S_i$ (Poisson statistics kept, no clipping)

## Attenuation correction: the phantom's attenuation in the system matrix

- The SRM was simulated in air; in the phantom, photons from deep inside are lost more than those near the surface
- For each voxel $j$ and module $m$: the fraction of photons surviving the straight path to the module's pinhole; every SRM row of that module is multiplied by it
- Path integrals through the phantom's own geometry and materials (water and the PMMA/nylon of walls, rods, spheres), traced with gammart (OptiX): 73 × 1.6 M rays in 8 s

$$A_{m,j} = \exp\left(-\int_{\mathbf r_j}^{\mathbf p_m} \mu(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}l\right), \qquad H^{\text{AC}}_{ij} = H_{ij}\,A_{m(i),j}$$

$\mu$ at 140.5 keV: water 0.154 /cm, PMMA 0.177 /cm. Checks: transmissions match exact analytic path lengths to 0.0013; the attenuated SRM predicts the unscattered projections with correlation 0.9996 (per-module totals 0.995–1.020; air SRM 0.79–1.10).

## The correction grows with depth; the PMMA inserts add about `{python} round(CM["inserts_share_median_pct"])` %

![](img/attenuation_correction_map.png){width=100%}

- Correction factor = air sensitivity ÷ attenuated sensitivity. In the water: `{python} f1(CM["correction_water_min"])`× at the wall, `{python} f1(CM["correction_centre"])`× at the FOV centre, up to `{python} f1(CM["correction_water_max"])`× at the lower centre of the phantom
- The cold inserts are in the attenuation model as PMMA; their share of the correction (vs an all-water phantom) is up to `{python} f1(CM["inserts_share_max_pct"])` %, median `{python} f1(CM["inserts_share_median_pct"])` %. Attenuation depends on material, not on activity

## Check: the attenuated SRM predicts the data; at 2 mm it misses at the phantom's edges

![](img/ac_pixel_residuals_2mm.png){width=78%}

::: {.smaller}
- **Test (no reconstruction):** forward-project the true phantom through the air SRM $H$ and the attenuated SRM $H \cdot A$, scale to the measured total, compare with the unscattered data pixel by pixel. $t$ = the pixel's transmission, $(H \cdot A)x / Hx$. Pearson residual $(y - \hat y)/\sqrt{\hat y}$: std 1 when only Poisson noise is left
- **Air:** modules `{python} f2(AR["2mm"]["air"]["module_ratio_min"])`–`{python} f2(AR["2mm"]["air"]["module_ratio_max"])`; data / model follows the water crossed (Pearson std `{python} f1(AR["2mm"]["air"]["pearson_std"])`)
- **$H \cdot A$, 2 mm:** modules `{python} f"{AR['2mm']['ac']['module_ratio_min']:.3f}"`–`{python} f"{AR['2mm']['ac']['module_ratio_max']:.3f}"`. Pixels with $t$ = 0.25–0.55 (`{python} pct(ar_bins("2mm", 0.25, 0.55)[2])` of the counts) agree within `{python} f"{ar_bins('2mm', 0.25, 0.55)[0]:.3f}"`–`{python} f"{ar_bins('2mm', 0.25, 0.55)[1]:.3f}"`; outside that range, where the rays graze the phantom's edge or cross the most water, the data are up to `{python} round((max(ar_bins("2mm", 0, 0.25)[1], ar_bins("2mm", 0.55, 1)[1]) - 1) * 100)` % above the model. Pearson std `{python} f2(AR["2mm"]["ac"]["pearson_std"])`
:::

## Check at 1 mm: the attenuated SRM matches the data within Poisson noise

![](img/ac_pixel_residuals_1mm.png){width=78%}

::: {.smaller}
- Same test with the 1 mm SRM, 1 mm attenuation factors and the phantom on the 1 mm grid: modules `{python} f"{AR['1mm']['ac']['module_ratio_min']:.3f}"`–`{python} f"{AR['1mm']['ac']['module_ratio_max']:.3f}"`, every transmission bin `{python} f"{ar_bins('1mm')[0]:.3f}"`–`{python} f"{ar_bins('1mm')[1]:.3f}"`, Pearson std `{python} f2(AR["1mm"]["ac"]["pearson_std"])`
- **One ray from the voxel to the pinhole centre is enough:** photons that reach the crystal through the collimator instead of the pinhole cause no measurable error
- **The 2 mm misfit is the grid:** activity and attenuation sampled on 2 mm voxels at the phantom's surfaces. This test cannot separate the two; in a reconstruction the activity is what is estimated, so the attenuation sampling is the part to fix (next: 2 mm SRM with factors averaged over each voxel)
- Caveat: the SRM and the data come from the same GATE physics, so this tests the attenuation model, not the physics
:::

# Reconstruction of the unscattered data

## The unscattered data: what the system matrix describes

- The simulation tags every photon that scattered in the phantom (Compton or Rayleigh); the **unscattered data** keep only the others: `{python} mc(TW["primary_main"])` of the `{python} mc(TW["main"])` main-window counts
- These photons may still scatter in the collimator or penetrate it, as in the SRM, so the SRM models them exactly apart from the phantom's attenuation
- This is the cleanest test of the reconstruction itself: no scatter correction needed, so only the support restriction and attenuation correction are left to study
- Next slides, 2 mm SRM: first the bare reconstruction in detail; then one change at a time, no corrections → + support restriction → + attenuation correction (AC), each at iterations 1–5, 20, 100 and 400

## Voxel values: why clip at 1.4× water {.smaller}

![](img/bare_histogram.png){width=86%}

- Every voxel with non-zero sensitivity, ÷ median water; dotted 1 (the median water), dashed 1.4 (the clip). Not drawn: voxels below 10⁻⁴ (`{python} n(BH["20"]["zero_voxels"])` at iteration 20, `{python} n(BH["400"]["zero_voxels"])` at 400)
- **Iteration 400:** the FOV edge (r ≥ 140 mm) holds `{python} pct(BH["400"]["FOV edge, r ≥ 140 mm"]["activity_share"])` of the activity, almost all in the `{python} f'{BH["400"]["FOV edge, r ≥ 140 mm"]["voxels_above_clip"] * 100:.1f} %'` of its voxels above the clip, up to `{python} f"{BH['400']['max']:,.0f}"`× water (at $(x, y, z)$ = (`{python} ', '.join(f'{v:.0f}' for v in BH['400']['max_at_mm'])`) mm, at the FOV edge next to the phantom's lid fittings); the phantom water holds `{python} pct(BH["400"]["phantom water"]["activity_share"])`. A linear scale to the maximum shows only these voxels
- **The clip:** the water peaks at 1 and the walls, inserts and the rest of the FOV lie below 1.4. But `{python} pct(BH["400"]["phantom water"]["voxels_above_clip"])` of the water voxels exceed it at iteration 400 (`{python} pct(BH["20"]["phantom water"]["voxels_above_clip"])` at 20; 99th percentile `{python} f1(BH["400"]["phantom water"]["p99"])`×): the bright rim without AC, which saturates white on the next slide; the line profiles give its true values

## What the unscattered data show

- With a matched model (unscattered photons, AC), MLEM returns the true activity (`{python} f2(U2["activity_over_truth"])`×) with a flat image (rim / centre `{python} f2(U2["rim_over_centre"])`) and almost nothing outside the phantom (`{python} pct(U2["outside_fraction"])`)
- Support restriction only cleans up the FOV edge; attenuation correction is what makes the image right
- Contrast and resolution are still limited by convergence: 7.9 mm rods `{python} f2(U2["rods_7.9mm"])`, FWHM `{python} f1(X["unscattered_fits"][UFIT["2: + support + AC"]]["400"]["25.4"]["fwhm_mm"])` mm at iteration 400, both still improving
- These numbers are the target for section 3: the full data with TEW scatter correction should get as close to them as possible ("ideal" row there)

## Activity outside the phantom: how to read the maximum-intensity projections

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](img/outside_mip.png){width=100%}
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- **What a panel is:** a maximum-intensity projection (MIP) of one 3D reconstruction: for every $(x, y)$, the *largest* voxel value along $z$ through the whole 288 mm FOV. Seen from above, $x$ to the right, $y$ up. One hot voxel anywhere in the column shows up, which a slice would miss
- **Grey scale:** 0 (black) to 1.4 × the median water value of that reconstruction. Everything at or above 1.4 × water is white, so the phantom (the central disc, 139 mm across) saturates, and *any* bright pixel outside it is activity that should not be there
- **Rows:** the correction steps, 0 none · 1 + support restriction · 2 + TEW · 3 + attenuation correction (2 mm SRM, full data)
- **Columns:** MLEM iterations 5, 20, 100 and 400
:::
::::

## Activity outside the phantom: what the projections show

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **Isolated white dots near the FOV edge** (row 0): single voxels the scanner barely sees, which MLEM drives up without bound, to $10^{5}\times$ water by iteration 400. Freezing low-sensitivity voxels (support restriction, row 1) removes them
- **Triangular streaks around the rim** (rows 0–2): present from the first iterations and still there after support restriction and TEW. They nearly vanish with attenuation correction (row 3): without AC the model cannot explain the counts lost to attenuation and puts them where few modules look
- **The phantom disc** sharpens with iterations; its halo at iteration 5 is the coarse early estimate
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
Share of the reconstructed activity more than 6 mm outside the phantom:

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(outside_table())
```

Early (it. 5): the blurred first estimate spills past the phantom edge in every row. Late (it. 100–400, rows 0–2): the hot edge voxels and rim streaks take over; only AC keeps the share falling.
:::
::::

[MIP: Wallis, IEEE Trans. Med. Imaging 8:297–303 (1989); Wallis & Miller, J. Nucl. Med. 32:534–546 (1991). The outside-phantom share is a diagnostic defined for this study.]{style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #777"}

## Statistical uncertainty: method {.smaller}

The contrasts above come from one noisy acquisition. To measure how much they would change with a new acquisition, the data were split into independent parts:

1. The `{python} n(1800)` simulation jobs (0.5 s time slices) were dealt into $K = 4$ **interleaved sub-acquisitions** (jobs 1, 5, 9, … ; 2, 6, 10, …): each covers the full 15 min with ¼ of the counts, and the four share no photons
2. Each sub-acquisition was merged and reconstructed exactly like the full data (TEW + AC, 2 mm and 1 mm SRMs, iteration 400), and its contrasts computed with the same masks

$$\bar C = \frac1K\sum_{k=1}^{K} C_k, \qquad s^2 = \frac{1}{K-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(C_k - \bar C\right)^2, \qquad \mathrm{SE}_{\text{full}} \approx \frac{s}{\sqrt K}$$

- $\mathrm{SE}_{\text{full}}$: standard error at the **full** count level; each part has $1/K$ of the counts and the variance scales about as 1/counts
- Grids compared **pairwise** on the same data: $d_k = C_k^{2\,\text{mm}} - C_k^{1\,\text{mm}}$, $\bar d \pm s_d/\sqrt K$, two-sided $t$-test of $\bar d = 0$ with $K - 1 = 3$ degrees of freedom. The noise common to both grids cancels, so small grid effects become visible
- Caveats: with $K = 4$ the standard errors themselves are uncertain by about ±40 %; the 1/counts scaling is approximate for MLEM at a fixed iteration

## Statistical uncertainty: contrast ± standard error

![](img/subset_errorbars_footprint.png){width=100%}

- Standard errors at full counts: rods `{python} se_text("rods")`; spheres 12.7–25.4 mm `{python} se_text("sphere", 12.7)`; spheres 6.4 and 9.5 mm `{python} se_text("sphere", 0, 9.5)` (only a few dozen voxels each): their single-number contrasts are the least reliable in this deck
- The 2 mm and 1 mm points overlap within their error bars for every insert

## Statistical uncertainty: the grids differ by less than the noise {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}

```{python}
print(subset_table())
```
:::

- **Differences** 2 − 1 mm: at most `{python} f"{subset_range()[2]:.3f}"` for any insert, in both directions; smaller than the contrast's own standard error everywhere except `{python} "; ".join(diff_exceeding_se()) or "none"`, where the 2 mm SRM is slightly higher
- The paired test is very sensitive (±0.001–0.005), so a few tiny differences come out "significant" (p < 0.05); with 12 inserts and two background definitions, a few such values are expected by chance
- The convex-hull rod background gives the same conclusion (largest difference `{python} f"{subset_range(mode='hull')[2]:.3f}"`)
- Sub-acquisition means agree with the full-data values (7.9 mm rods: `{python} f"{SUB['per_grid']['footprint']['2mm']['400']['rods_7.9mm']['mean']:.3f}"` vs `{python} f2(M["2mm_step3_ac"]["full_tew"]["400"]["rods_7.9mm"])`)
:::
::::

## Why the grid does not matter for this scanner

- The system blurs more than the grid: fitted FWHM `{python} f1(fwhm("resolution", "2 mm", 400))`–`{python} f1(fwhm("resolution", "1 mm", 400))` mm at iteration 400 with every grid; a 2 mm grid already represents detail down to about 4 mm
- MLEM is not converged: contrast still rises at iteration 400, and noise-free and measured curves almost coincide, so iterations, not counts or voxels, limit the image
- A finer grid costs more and is noisier: 1 mm takes 5.5× the time per iteration and 28 GB instead of 8.6 GB, and each SRM entry comes from 8× fewer simulated photons
- Would change the answer: sharper system resolution (smaller pinholes, finer detector pixels) or tasks on structures of 4 mm or less

## Caveats and next steps

**Caveats**

- Simulation only: the SRM and the data share geometry and physics
- The $\mu$ map is the exact phantom; real data need a CT or a fitted outline
- One ray per voxel and module (pinhole centre); plain MLEM, no regularisation; cold inserts only

**Next steps**

- Same pipeline on the corrected XCAT head data (running on Expanse); 42 % of its counts come from outside the FOV
- Scatter: model the TEW estimate $s$ inside MLEM, comparing $y$ with $H\lambda + s$, instead of subtracting it ($y - s$ vs $H\lambda$): keeps the Poisson statistics, no clipping, less noise
- OSEM or another accelerated algorithm; a hot-sphere phantom for recovery coefficients
